page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 20 vCPUs and 20 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. The server includes three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 4190.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 3088.0, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, scoring 84070.24 in stress-ng and 17663.0 in Geekbench. Memory performance is also highly rated, with a Passmark memory score in the top 10% and large-block read bandwidth reaching 306.94 GB/sec. Text processing and single-threaded compression benchmarks also rank in the top 10%, while ray tracing performance falls in the middle 50%.

The primary hardware tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU resources combined with 256 GB of RAM provides a specialized profile for parallel computing workloads. This configuration is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning model training, large-scale data processing, and rendering tasks that leverage the Ada Lovelace architecture, while general database operations are supported by a strong Passmark database score of 27020.33.
